label: the loop runs its body once rather than while the test holds
the entry guard admits a cursor equal to the limit
the entry guard is the wrong way round
the limit is read once rather than every pass
why: 0x62925 loads the limit into %dx before the loop and every rejoin block reloads it -- 0x629cf, 0x62d70, 0x63948, 0x640a1 and 0x64326 are all `movzwl 0x2aa0(reg),%edx` -- so the object re-reads it every pass and finding 710 says so. It cannot be OBSERVED to, because NOTHING WRITES +0x2aa0 while the loop is running: the five references in the loop's whole span 0x62950..0x64518 are those five reads, v34hstx1.cpp never assigns f2aa0, and the only write in src/ is v34handshakinit's `= 6` during bring-up. A cached limit and a re-read limit are therefore the same value on every pass. Recorded equivalent rather than left uncaught, and the `while` keeps the object's form. Finding 714.

label: the transmit state is read as unsigned rather than signed
why: 0x62957 is `movswl 0x3596(%esi),%eax` and the sign IS forced -- the object could have used `movzwl` and did not. But the two readings agree over EVERY value the halfword can hold, so no differential test can separate them, and this is recorded equivalent rather than left as a silent uncaught. The range test is `sub $0x5,%eax; cmp $0x51,%eax; ja`, an UNSIGNED compare against 0x51: for a state in 0..0x7fff the two extensions are the same integer, and for a negative one the signed reading gives (s - 5), whose unsigned value is at least 0xffff7ffb, while the zero-extended reading gives (0x10000 + s - 5), which is at least 0x7ffb. Both are far above 0x51, so both take the loop bottom. The declared type is what keeps our `movswl` -- `hs_get` returns short -- and the codegen tier is what would see it move, not this one. Finding 714.
